batch: Exodus scenes indices 25–36 derived from registry JSON

scenes.title: Israel under oppression
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Pharaoh; Hebrew midwives Shiphrah and Puah; Hebrew people collectively
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 1:8–22 describes a new Pharaoh's oppression and order to kill Hebrew boys; no route or precise city is supplied. Goshen is linked in wider Genesis/Exodus context, but this passage says the Israelites multiplied in Egypt and names no Goshen location.

geography.claim: Egypt country-level; Goshen only contextual from other passages, not stated in 1:8–22. No exact location.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: No genealogy; oppression precedes Moses' birth and Exodus deliverance.

scenes.title: Moses is born and hidden
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Unnamed Levite man/woman, infant Moses, Moses' sister, Pharaoh's daughter, her maidens, Hebrew nurse
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 2:1–10 narrates Moses' birth, concealment, basket on Nile bank among reeds, Pharaoh's daughter finding him, and his sister arranging a Hebrew nurse. It is an exact Atlas reference match, but no city is stated.

geography.claim: Nile riverbank/reeds are textual; Nile delta/valley only regional inference. Specific bank unknown.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Moses' Levitical parentage is stated in adjacent context (2:1); no covenant act.

scenes.title: Moses flees to Midian
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Moses; Egyptian; Hebrew disputants; Reuel/Jethro; his daughters; Zipporah
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 2:11–22 covers Moses' killing of Egyptian, flight, and residence in Midian; Jethro's daughters and Zipporah are named later within the span. No single location for the whole sequence; the flight route is unstated.

geography.claim: Egypt, Midian textual regions. Midian's extent/modern location is broad and debated; no point pin or route.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Moses marries Zipporah and becomes father of Gershom (2:21–22); no covenant event.

scenes.title: The burning bush
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Moses; God/LORD; angel of the LORD in flame; Jethro mentioned as owner/kin
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 3:1–15 places Moses at Horeb, the mountain of God, while tending Jethro's flock. Burning bush, divine call, and name revelation are narrated; Jebel Musa is later tradition and not established by text.

geography.claim: Horeb named by text, but modern mountain identification contested; classify TEXTUAL_NAME / TRADITIONAL_SITE_CANDIDATE. Not exact coordinate.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Call of Moses initiates deliverance; promise to patriarchs invoked (3:6,15), covenant continuity explicit.

scenes.title: Moses returns to Egypt
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Moses, Zipporah, sons (unnamed), LORD/angel context, Aaron, Israelite elders
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 4:18–31 narrates Moses' return to Egypt, encounter at lodging place with Zipporah's circumcision action, Aaron's meeting, signs, and elders' belief. Registry Goshen label is not stated in this passage.

geography.claim: Moses leaves Midian for Egypt; exact lodging, route and meeting place unspecified. Egypt regional only.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Moses/Zipporah family; circumcision is covenant sign in narrative context; elders' worship responds to deliverance announcement.

scenes.title: Let my people go
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Moses, Aaron, Pharaoh, Israelite foremen, taskmasters
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 5:1–23 is Pharaoh's court confrontation and increased labor burden. Rameses is not named in this passage; the city marker is a hypothesis and should not be represented as exact.

geography.claim: Egypt; court/city not named. Rameses hypothesis is unsupported by cited verses.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Deliverance conflict within covenant promise to Israel; no genealogy.

scenes.title: The staff and the magicians
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 7:8–13 is a sign before Pharaoh, not the first plague. Aaron's staff becomes a serpent and consumes the magicians' staffs; the registry title is accurate, but location Rameses is not specified.

geography.claim: Pharaoh's presence/court implied; no city or exact location in verses.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Deliverance signs; no genealogy or covenant enactment.

scenes.title: The first plague: the Nile turns to blood
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 7:14–25 narrates the Nile water sign/plague and seven-day interval. Text names river, canals, ponds, pools and vessels; no single reach of Nile is identified. The scene's first-plague description is text-faithful.

geography.claim: Nile and waters in Egypt exact at regional feature level; no exact river location.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Plague begins confrontation; no covenant/genealogy event.

scenes.title: The first Passover
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: LORD, Moses, Aaron, Israelite households collectively, firstborn/household members
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 12:1–28 includes Passover instruction, household lamb/blood, meal, and Israel's observance in Egypt; it is not just a single location event. Keep household-scale activity, no registry pin beyond regional Egypt/Goshen.

geography.claim: Egypt; household doorways across Israelite settlements, not one point. Goshen may contextualize from Exodus 8:22 but not sole site from these verses.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Passover institution becomes covenantal memorial; household generations and instruction to children explicit in vv24–27.

scenes.title: The departure from Rameses
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Moses, Aaron, Pharaoh, Israelite people, mixed multitude; Egyptians collectively
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 12:31–42 narrates Pharaoh's release command and Israel's departure from Rameses, with 600,000 men and mixed multitude; the route starts at Rameses per v37. Rameses is explicit here, unlike 5:1.

geography.claim: Rameses named as departure point (12:37), exact archaeological departure point and route unknown. Registry's eastern Delta label remains regional/hypothetical.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Israel leaves after Passover; firstborn judgment and deliverance memorial context. Genealogical age/sojourning summary in vv40–41 is textual chronology.

scenes.title: The pillar of cloud and fire
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: LORD; Israel collectively; Moses only implicit in narrative
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 13:17–22 describes God directing the route away from Philistine road, cloud/fire pillar, and encampment at Etham on edge of wilderness. It does not name the northern Suez isthmus; that is modern route hypothesis.

geography.claim: Succoth, Etham named in surrounding itinerary (13:20); 13:17–22 route features but sea-crossing site unresolved. Regional/topographic sequence, not a precise line.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Deliverance sequence and divine guidance; Joseph's bones carried from 13:19 (ancestral link).

scenes.title: The crossing of the sea
scenes.personsExplicitOrCollective: Moses, LORD, angel of God, Israel collectively, Pharaoh's chariots/army, Egyptians collectively
scenes.chronologyAndNarrativeFinding: Exodus 14:15–31 describes sea crossing, Egyptian pursuit, divided waters, Israel's passage, destruction of Egyptian force. Text does not identify the body of water by a modern name; keep location unestablished.

geography.claim: Sea crossing exact event in text, modern site UNKNOWN; Suez/Reed Sea identifications disputed. No pin or route.

scenes.covenantAndGenealogy: Deliverance from Egypt; follows Passover and pillar; covenant Sinai follows later. No named genealogy.

openQuestions: Modern identification of Horeb/Sinai remains traditional and contested.
The Exodus sea-crossing location and route remain unresolved; source text provides no modern cartographic identification.
Goshen is not named in Exodus 1:8–22, 2:1–10, or 4:18–31; do not transfer a regional contextual label as verse-level location.
